newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubin, MOF agree G7 forex stance unchanged - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Rubin, MOF agree G7 forex stance unchanged - MOF.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka discussed the issue of foreign exchange rates with U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Friday and they agreed that the Group of Seven (G7) stance on foreign exchange rates remains unchanged, a senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official told Reuters.
"The two sides agreed to cooperate in economic and financial areas, and cooperation in foreign exchange is a part of that," said the Japanese official, who attended the meeting.
The G7 nations agreed at a meeting in Berlin in February that major misalignments in exchange rates, noted in a G7 communique in April 1995, had been corrected.

The G7 nations also affirmed at the February meeting that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excess volatility was undesirable. They agreed to monitor developments in currency markets and to cooperate as appropriate.
But Mitsuzuka said after the meeting with Rubin that there were no specific discussions on currencies.
